land.text: the Ordos fringe round Yinzhou held by Li Jiqian's Tangut holdouts; Jipeng gave up the Dingnan Jiedushi to the Song in 982

predecessors.note: Li Jiqian refused to submit in 982, captured Yinzhou in 985 and accepted the title 'King of the Xia State' from the Liao in 990; the Western Xia infobox dates the dynasty from 1038 (Jingzong). Cliopatria starts the row in 990.

land.text: the Xia core round Yinchuan; the Hexi corridor had been taken in 1226

successors.note: Emperor Mo surrendered in September 1227 and was executed; the Mongols then 'pillaged the capital'.

capitals.name: Yinzhou (Li Jiqian's base)
capitals.note: Approximate site. The pages opened give no capital before 1038 (Jiqian captured Yinzhou in 985; his brother's Dingnan base was Xiazhou); Cliopatria's shape for these years is the Ordos edge.

capitals.name: Xingqing (Zhongxing, Yinchuan)
capitals.note: 'In 1038 Yuanhao set up his capital there' (Xingqing, modern Yinchuan); the page calls it Zhongxing in the 1209 siege. It fell to the Mongols in 1227.

rulers.name: Li Jiqian
rulers.note: King of the Xia State from 990 (Liao title); died of an arrow wound on 6 January 1004. Rebelled against the Song from 982/984.

rulers.name: Li Deming
rulers.note: Succeeded Jiqian in 1004; 'sent tribute missions to both the Liao dynasty and the Song dynasty'. Yuanhao succeeded him in 1032.

rulers.name: Jingzong (Li Yuanhao)
rulers.note: Table: 1038-1048 as emperor; ruled from 1032; stabbed on 19 January 1048.

rulers.name: Mo (Li Xian)
rulers.note: The table gives no temple name; the text calls him Emperor Mo. Surrendered in September 1227.

keyframe_review.note: 113.5 thousand km2 round the Ordos edge (106-112.6 E, 37.8-41.1 N): the Tangut land of Li Jiqian, who took Yinzhou in 985 and the Liao title 'King of the Xia State' in 990. No page opened gives an area for these years.

correction.text: the Ordos core plus Liangzhou (Wuwei), annexed in 1032

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'In 1032, Yuanhao annexed the Tibetan confederation of Xiliangfu' (Liangzhou/Wuwei); the Guiyi Circuit surrendered about 1030 and the Ganzhou Uyghur Kingdom fell by 1036. Cliopatria adds the whole Hexi corridor only in 1040.

Cliopatria's unchanged shape for 1034-1039 is wrong: 'by 1036 he had annexed both the Ganzhou Uyghur Kingdom and the Guiyi Circuit'. The 1040 shape applies from 1036 (1032-1035 is the new keyframe above).

473.6 thousand km2: Ordos, Alxa and the Hexi corridor (96.3-112.6 E). The infobox gives about 1.0 M km2 for 1100 and the body 'at its peak, about 800,000 km2' (the two figures conflict); Cliopatria's 0.47 M km2 is 0.47 and 0.59 of them, so beyond a factor of two on the infobox figure. The shape is kept: Ningxia, Gansu, eastern Qinghai, northern Shaanxi and the Mongolian edge are named as the empire's regions and the shape omits the Gansu and Qinghai fringe. The wars of 1039-1044 and 1081-1085 did not move the frontier on the pages opened.
473.6 thousand km2, no change; Chongzong 'declared himself a vassal of Jin in 1124' (Jin page).
474.4 thousand km2; the Jin ceded the Qingtang (Xining) area to the Xia in 1136 (Tsongkha page), outside this shape (confidence 2).
471.4 thousand km2. Mongol raids of 1205 (Edsin), 1207 (Ordos Plateau, Wuhai) and 1209 (siege of the capital, flood) took no land; the Xia submitted in January 1210.

Cliopatria drops the Hexi corridor in 1216 (110 thousand km2), but the Mongol pages date no loss before 1226: the 1217 siege of the capital ended in withdrawal and Genghis took 'Suzhou ... five weeks', 'Ganzhou five months' and Liangzhou ('surrendered without resistance in August 1226') in 1225-1226. The 1206 shape applies to 1216-1225.
110 thousand km2: the Yinchuan and Ordos core left after the Hexi campaign of 1226 ('in November lay siege to Lingwu, a mere 30 kilometers from Yinchuan'); valid 1226-1227 instead of 1220-1226.

region.text: the Tangut land of Li Jiqian on the Ordos edge

ledger.note: 990: Li Jiqian takes the Liao title 'King of the Xia State'. In 982 his brother Jipeng gave the Dingnan Jiedushi to the Song and Jiqian refused; 'in 984, the Song attacked his camp'; he 'captured Yinzhou in 985', paid tribute to the Liao from 986, married a Khitan noble in 989 and 'in 990 accepted the title'. The infobox dates the dynasty to 1038.
1028: Yuanhao attacks Ganzhou. 'In 1028, he sent his son Yuanhao to conquer the Ganzhou Uyghur Kingdom' (Western Xia page).
1032: Yuanhao annexes Liangzhou. 'In 1032, Yuanhao annexed the Tibetan confederation of Xiliangfu.' The Xiliangfu dossier ends the state in 1016.
1036: the Ganzhou Uyghurs are annexed: 'by 1036 he had annexed both the Ganzhou Uyghur Kingdom and the Guiyi Circuit'.
1036: the fighting at Ganzhou ends in annexation.

1036: the Guiyi Circuit is annexed. The Western Xia page has it surrender 'two years after 1028' (about 1030); the Song-Xia wars page says 'by 1036 he had annexed both'; the Guiyi dossier uses 1036. The Tangut script was disseminated in 1036.
1038: Yuanhao declares himself emperor of the Great Xia. 'In 1038, Yuanhao declared himself emperor of the Great Xia'; infobox: established 1038. The Song cut border trade.
1038: the capital is Xingqing (Yinchuan). 'In 1038 Yuanhao set up his capital there.'

Winter 1039-40: Yuanhao besieges Yanzhou. 'Winter 1039-1040: Yuanhao besieged Yanzhou'; Liu Ping's 9,000 men were beaten at Sanchuan Pass by 50,000 Xia troops and Ren Fu's 30,000 were annihilated at Haoshuichuan; Dingchuan was surrounded in 1042.

1044: peace. After the failed Liao invasion of 1044 'Yuanhao made peace. The Song recognized his rights to Xia lands as king and agreed to an annual tribute of 250,000 units of silk, silver, and tea'.

1081: the five-pronged Song attack. Lanzhou fell in October 1081 and the Xia abandoned the middle Ordos and Xiazhou in November; on 21 December the Xia breached the Yellow River dikes and flooded the Song camps.
October 1081: Lanzhou falls to the Song. The page lists it as a Song gain in this war; Cliopatria's Xia shape never includes it.

April 1085: the war ends on Shenzong's death. Xia had besieged Yongle in September 1082 (300,000 men; 17,300 Song lost) and failed at Lanzhou in 1083 and January 1084; 'the Song returned four of the six captured towns' for 100 prisoners.

1113: the Xia 'took the Qingtang region' (Song-Xia wars page). The Tsongkha page has the Song prince Zhao Huaide there in 1108 and the Jin ceding the area to the Xia in 1136; the pages disagree and the Cliopatria shape never includes it.
1136: the Jin cede the Tsongkha country. 'The Jin dynasty, which had conquered the area, ceded it to Western Xia' (Tsongkha page, 1136).

region.text: the Mongol approach from the Ordos to the capital

ledger.note: 1209: Genghis invades. 'In 1209, Genghis undertook his campaign to actually conquer Western Xia'; he took Wulahai after beating Gao Lianghui and besieged the capital until a dike broke and flooded the Mongol camp (earlier raids: 1205 in the Edsin region, 1207 into the Ordos and Wuhai).

region.text: the Mongol approach to the capital

ledger.note: January 1210: Xiangzong submits. 'Emperor Xiangzong of Western Xia surrendered to the Mongols in January 1210', giving a daughter and a tribute of camels, falcons and textiles; the Mongol ledger records the vassalage.

union.text: Hexi corridor and Alxa: Liangzhou, Ganzhou, Suzhou, Guazhou

region.text: the Hexi corridor and the Yinchuan plain

ledger.note: 1225: Genghis returns. 'In 1225, Genghis Khan attacked with a force of approximately 180,000' because the emperor refused to join the Khwarazm campaign in 1219.

region.text: Hexi corridor and Alxa: Liangzhou, Ganzhou, Suzhou, Guazhou

ledger.note: 1226: the Hexi corridor falls. Suzhou 'fell after five weeks', Ganzhou took 'five months'; in August 1226 Genghis moved on Wuwei and Liangzhou 'surrendered without resistance'; in November he besieged Lingwu, 30 km from Yinchuan. Only Liangzhou is dated by month; the year 1226 is used for the whole corridor.

union.text: Hexi corridor and Alxa: Liangzhou, Ganzhou, Suzhou, Guazhou

region.text: the Hexi corridor and the Yinchuan plain

ledger.note: September 1227: Emperor Mo surrenders. 'Upon reaching Yinchuan in 1227 and setting siege to the city', which was besieged 'for about six months'; Genghis died in August 1227 (one section says December); 'in September 1227, Emperor Mozhu surrendered to the Mongols and was promptly executed'.
September 1227: the Western Xia end. 'The destruction of Western Xia during the second campaign was near total'; the capital was pillaged and its people massacred.

wars.name: Li Jiqian's revolt against the Song
wars.outcome: Jiqian resisted Song control from 982, was attacked in 984, took Yinzhou in 985, accepted the Liao title in 990, raided Lingzhou in May 996 and November 997, accepted Song suzerainty briefly after 998 and died on 6 January 1004.
wars.note: Page: Lingzhou raids in May 996 and November 997.

wars.name: Xia conquest of the Hexi corridor

zones.text: Hexi corridor and Alxa: Liangzhou, Ganzhou, Suzhou, Guazhou

wars.outcome: Liangzhou annexed 1032; Guiyi Circuit about 1030-1036; the Ganzhou Uyghur Kingdom by 1036; Tangut script 1036.

wars.name: Song-Xia war of 1038-1044
wars.outcome: Xia victories at Sanchuan Pass, Haoshuichuan and Dingchuan; Liao invasion of 1044 failed; peace with the Song paying 250,000 units of silk, silver and tea yearly.

wars.name: Liao-Xia wars
wars.outcome: Liao invasions of 1044 (100,000 men) and the later 1049-1050 invasions failed to take the capital; peace by 1053.
wars.note: The Liao page dates the second invasion to 1048, the Western Xia page to 1049 and 1050.

wars.name: Song-Xia war of 1081-1085
wars.outcome: Song took Lanzhou (October 1081) and six towns; Xia flooded the Song camps, took Yongle (September 1082) and held Lanzhou against attacks; four of six towns returned in 1085.
wars.note: Wars resumed 1097-1099 (40 Song forts), 1103-1105 and 1113-1119 (ceasefire and Huizong's apology in 1119).

wars.name: Mongol conquest of Western Xia

zones.text: Hexi corridor and Alxa: Liangzhou, Ganzhou, Suzhou, Guazhou

wars.outcome: Raids 1205 and 1207; siege of the capital 1209 and submission in January 1210; Xia attacked the Jin in 1210 and joined the Mongols against them in 1211; refusal of troops in 1217 and 1219; the Hexi campaign of 1226; siege of Yinchuan 1227 and surrender in September 1227.

certainty.note: Desert, steppe and mountain frontiers throughout; the Song frontier was recognised in 1044 but the 1099 peace was 'unable to clearly demarcate' it (Song-Xia wars page).

sources.title: Western Xia
sources.note: Identity, capital, rulers, Hexi conquests 1028-1036, Mongol campaigns.

sources.title: Tsongkha
sources.note: The Jin cession of the Qingtang area to the Xia, 1136.

sources.title: Liao dynasty
sources.note: Used for the Liao invasions of Western Xia (1044, 1048) in the war note only.

sources.title: Jin dynasty (1115-1234)
sources.note: Chongzong's vassalage to the Jin in 1124.

notes:
Cliopatria's Western Xia row starts in 990 and ends in 1226; the dossier runs 990-1227 (Emperor Mo surrendered in September 1227). The state's infobox dates the dynasty from 1038 (Jingzong's imperial title); 990 (the Liao title) is used for the birth, with the 982 refusal, the 985 capture of Yinzhou and the 1038 proclamation in the notes and events.

Shape problems: (1) the Hexi corridor appears in one step at 1040 although Liangzhou fell in 1032, Guiyi about 1030-1036 and Ganzhou by 1036 (new keyframes); (2) the 1216 step removes the Hexi corridor ten years too early: the Mongol pages date its loss to 1226; (3) the 110 thousand km2 shape applies to 1226-1227 only. The infobox area (about 1.0 M km2 in 1100; the body says 800,000 km2 at its peak) is 1.7 to 2.1 times Cliopatria's 0.47 M km2; the shape was kept.

Not settled: the capital before 1038 (no page); the Xiliangfu dossier ends that state in 1016 while this page has Yuanhao annexing it in 1032; the Guiyi date (about 1030 on the Xia page, 1036 on the Song-Xia page and in the Guiyi dossier); Qingtang changing hands in 1113 (Song-Xia wars page) against the Song prince at Qingtang in 1108 and the Jin ceding it in 1136 (Tsongkha page); the day the capital fell (the Mongol page gives August 1227 and December for Genghis's death); the Jin vassalage is dated 1124 on the Jin page (Cliopatria 1126). The Liao and Song both received Xia tribute (986/990 Liao title; 1044 Song recognition) but neither page calls it vassalage; the Jin vassalage and the Mongol submission of 1210 are recorded in their ledgers. Need dossiers elsewhere: none new.
